checks.question: Does shared media have one owner and consume only declared shared/browser dependencies?
checks.detail: Both readers and their matching tests live in music-workbench, with core and the browser codec declared dependencies. No runtime app, GM, Tauri, Node or host-fetch import is present in the inspected media module. This is a local import review, not a whole production dependency-graph acceptance.

checks.question: Is HTTP injected, and are media codecs excluded from the inspected workbench root entry?
checks.detail: runtimeHttpClient delegates to configured WorkbenchRuntime.http; the root does not statically import either media reader or Mediabunny. Range codec construction occurs in the explicit media subpath. Transitive root graph and failed dynamic-import retry are outside this subbatch.

checks.question: Are Range bytes verifiable, fanout bounded and cancelled sessions prevented from publishing?
checks.detail: Seven supplemental expectations fail across three confirmed P2 findings: unbounded eager chunk fanout/no sibling cancellation in the reader, acceptance of unverifiable 206 ranges and byte delivery after cancellation/disposal. Coalesced size probes, one-only redirected-URL retry and full-read pre-cancellation pass. Existing tests additionally cover per-request bounds/headers, small complete-response reuse, backup selection and forwarding disposal to HTTP.

checks.question: Does the inspected shared layer retain transport/account authority behind injected ports?
checks.detail: Requests use bytes, explicit include for built-ins and omit for the existing custom-* branch, response byte limits, timeouts and the portable cancellation contract. No raw account credentials or storage writes occur in these readers. Native enforcement and actual GM/Rust cancellation/limits are unknown; the custom-* branch is not evidence of supported S15 external media.

checks.question: Do owner tests provide matching behavioral evidence for the selected contract?
checks.detail: The two existing files pass 7/7 and workbench typecheck passes. The corrected supplemental probe passes 3/10 and fails 7/10, revealing gaps in the original suite. Probe source/logs are retained locally and its temporary repository file was removed. No product implementation or permanent test was changed.

callChain.detail: Two direct consumers construct a session-scoped Mediabunny Input using createRangeMediaSource and a cancellation signal; failure paths dispose Input. Full player control flow was not reviewed.

CustomSource owns the session reader with a 16 MiB codec cache. getSize coalesces a one-byte Range probe; reads split into 2 MiB HTTP requests. Small HTTP 200 probe results are reused in session memory.
Media requests delegate to runtime.http; adapter is responsible for honoring byte caps, timeout and cancellation. The owning GM/Rust adapter was not followed.

Range assembly and full-file fallback return bytes. dispose aborts the signal, but post-settlement result validation and cache invalidation are incomplete. Caller-level stale playback takeover has not been demonstrated.

static.detail: Local owner/import/call-chain review confirms the three findings. All 16 captured source/config/dependency inputs remained unchanged.

findings.title: Range reads fan out every chunk before any result, without a reader-owned concurrency bound
findings.trigger: A decoder requests a large byte interval; read(0, 32 MiB) is the deterministic reproduction.
findings.effect: The loop starts ceil(intervalBytes / 2 MiB) requests immediately: 16 requests before any settlement in the probe. The per-request 2 MiB cap and codec 16 MiB cache do not limit aggregate in-flight bytes or request count. If one fails, the reader does not cancel siblings; downstream Input disposal can terminate them, so a production leak beyond consumer cleanup is not established.
findings.suggestedNextAction: Use a reader-owned bounded chunk scheduler with cancellation of the failed read group. Preserve chunk order and per-response byte limits; test large spans, out-of-order completion, failure stopping new work and cancellation. Do not interpret Mediabunny's two callback workers as an HTTP chunk limit.

findings.title: 206 range validation accepts missing or internally contradictory Content-Range
findings.trigger: read(10,14) receives four bytes with HTTP 206 and either no Content-Range or Content-Range: bytes 10-99/50.
findings.effect: Both responses are returned successfully. responseStart is optional, and the declared end/total are never checked in requestRange. Bytes whose requested identity cannot be verified may reach the decoder as if they were the correct interval; playback/decode corruption or unnecessary fallback is possible. No real upstream server exhibiting these responses was tested.
findings.suggestedNextAction: Parse a required complete Content-Range for 206 responses and validate safe integer start/end/total, requested interval and body length; bind total to the known probe size as appropriate. Reject malformed/missing/mismatched ranges with media-range-invalid.

findings.title: Cancellation does not reject settled HTTP results or disposed-reader cached bytes
findings.trigger: HTTP has already fulfilled, then abort/dispose occurs synchronously before the reader await continuation; alternatively dispose after a successful small complete-response probe and read its cache.
findings.effect: Range reads and complete-file loading still fulfill with bytes after cancellation; a disposed reader also serves cached bytes. This does not require an HTTP adapter to ignore cancellation: its promise was fulfilled before abort. The reader has no post-await cancellation check and dispose does not clear cached bytes. The probe establishes a media-port lifecycle violation; it does not prove that a higher-level player or exporter lacks its own freshness guard.
findings.suggestedNextAction: Reject reads at entry and after asynchronous transport settlement when the session is cancelled; check before returning cached bytes, and release session caches on dispose. Add cancellation-before-continuation and disposed-cache regressions without relying only on transport abort notifications.

handoff.summary: B07-media-shared has three open P2 findings and is violating/needs-fix. Original 7 tests and typecheck pass, while 7 of 10 corrected supplemental expectations fail. The shared injection boundary and bounded per-request options are present, but aggregate fanout, exact 206 validation and post-cancellation delivery are incomplete. All 16 hashed inputs remain unchanged and this audit changed no product files. Unrelated contribution-registry edits and B06 report files appeared concurrently and were preserved. Other five B07 candidates, production artifacts and both runtime acceptances remain unreviewed.
